extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing creative writers looking for an online peer-critique workshop
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and site rules for participating in Critique Circle: how to earn submission credits by critiquing others, submit stories for review, use critiques to revise, and manage story privacy and membership. Focus is on reciprocal peer feedback within the community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocity (critique others to receive critiques)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique the stories of others and in turn they will crit your stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site emphasizes reciprocity: you must crit a couple of stories to gain enough credits before submitting your own. ('Crit a couple of stories to gain enough credits.') This is the primary mechanism to participate and receive feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit-based submission system
rubrics_metrics.description: Use your credits to submit your own story for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitting a story for critique requires spending credits earned by critiquing other members' work. ('Use your credits to submit your own story for review.') The three-step flow is: 1) Crit, 2) Submit, 3) Rewrite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative revision using received critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the crits to improve your manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receiving critiques, authors are expected to revise: 'Use the crits to improve your manuscript.' The site frames this as continuous improvement through giving and receiving critiques and building relationships with other authors who will help you with your manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manageable privacy and non-publication of submitted stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories submitted to CC are not considered 'published online' and cannot be found on search engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors retain control over accessibility and may delete stories at any time: 'You can manage your story accessibility yourself and delete them at any time.' This policy is presented to reassure writers concerned about online publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership model (free + optional premium)
rubrics_metrics.description: Membership is free and always has been. There is also a premium subscription that you can buy which unlocks additional features and perks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic participation (including critiquing and submitting via credits) is available to free members; paying members receive extra features. No further pricing or feature details are provided on the landing page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Active community engagement (forums and groups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Active forums: Discussion groups on nearly any topic under any sun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site encourages participation in forums and discussion groups as part of community engagement. It positions itself as a 'vibrant writing community' with 'thousands of writers working together to improve their writing.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on quality, helpful critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique Circle claims high-quality reviews and reviewers who provide substantive feedback rather than superficial praise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testimonials highlight that members give constructive, knowledgeable critiques (e.g., 'This is not one of those sites that you can post your writing and readers give you a "good job, keep up the good work!"'). While promotional, this communicates an implicit expectation that critiques should be substantive and helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Member-authored instructional resources (blog on craft)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Critique Circle blog is written by our members and is filled with interesting articles about writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blog provides craft-focused articles (examples on the landing page include world-building and using unity of effect) that participants can read to improve their writing and inform critiques.
